request.description:
Get one end user.

`GET /v1/users/{id}`

Hard-delete an end user.

`DELETE /v1/users/{id}`

The user's status becomes `deleting` at once: reads of their data return 404 and
the user's tokens stop working, so uploads get 401 (410 only for an upload whose
token was accepted just before). A background job then revokes provider connections (best effort),
deletes the user's raw files and every row of the user, then the user.
`GET /v1/deletions/{job_id}` tells when it is done.

Status of a deletion.

`GET /v1/deletions/{job_id}`

Poll until `status` is `done`: the user's raw files and rows are gone (with `provider`
set, only those of that provider). The job is kept after the user is deleted. Another
tenant's job is a 404.

variable.description:
The `job_id` returned by `DELETE /v1/users/{id}`, `DELETE /v1/users/{id}/data/{provider}`
or `DELETE /v1/users/{id}/connections/{provider}?delete_data=true`.

item.name: Erase a user's data from one provider

request.description:
Erase a user's data from one provider.

`DELETE /v1/users/{id}/data/{provider}`

Erases everything the user holds from one provider without touching any connection:
the route for device providers (`apple_health`, `health_connect`), which have no
connection, and for a provider already disconnected. A background job deletes every
record, raw file and sync record of this user and provider; the user and their other
providers stay. The answer is 202 with the `job_id` to poll at
`GET /v1/deletions/{job_id}`; asking again while it runs returns the same job. Until
it is done, uploads of that provider for the user are refused (409). A provider the
user is still connected to is a 409: use
`DELETE /v1/users/{id}/connections/{provider}?delete_data=true`. A provider unknown to
this build is a 404.

variable.description: Connector slug, see GET /v1/providers.

request.description:
Mint a user token.

`POST /v1/users/{id}/tokens`

Returns an opaque `ohs_ut_` token for one active user, shown only in this response
(`Cache-Control: no-store`). Lifetime: one hour by default, at most 24 hours; a token
whose only scope is `read` may live up to 30 days (2592000 s), for a person's own AI
agent configuration (MCP). `Idempotency-Key` is ignored here.

Register a webhook endpoint.

`POST /v1/webhooks`

The endpoint receives a signed POST for each event of `event_types` (empty or absent:
every type). The response carries the signing `secret` (`whsec_...`), shown only here
(`Cache-Control: no-store`). The URL must be https and must not point at a private,
loopback or link-local address, unless the instance sets `OHS_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true`.
At most 20 endpoints per tenant. `Idempotency-Key` is ignored here. See docs/webhooks.md.

The tenant's webhook endpoints.

`GET /v1/webhooks`

Oldest first, on one page (`next_cursor` is always null).

One webhook endpoint.

`GET /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}`

Change a webhook endpoint.

`PATCH /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}`

Absent fields stay as they are. `enabled: false` disables the endpoint and parks its
pending deliveries; `enabled: true` re-activates it (also after an automatic disable)
and clears its failure state.

Delete a webhook endpoint.

`DELETE /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}`

The endpoint and its deliveries are deleted; nothing more is sent to it.

Replace the signing secret.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/rotate-secret`

The new secret signs every request from now on, retries of earlier events included.
Shown only in this response.

Send a test event.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/test`

Queues a test event for this endpoint alone, whatever its event types. Without a body (or
with `event_type` `webhook.test`) it is the generic `webhook.test` event. With another
`event_type` it is a realistic sample of that event, about no real user (`user_id` is the
nil UUID, `external_ref` is `sample-user`). Either payload carries `"test": true`.

The endpoint's deliveries.

`GET /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries`

Newest first (unlike the data lists). Finished deliveries are kept 30 days.

query.description: The next_cursor of the previous page.

item.name: One delivery with its payload and attempts

request.description:
One delivery with its payload and attempts.

`GET /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}`

The delivery, the exact JSON body it sends (`payload`) and its attempts, oldest first: status
code, error, timing and the first 1 KiB of the receiver's answer. The last 20 attempts
are kept.

item.name: Send a finished delivery's event again, as a new delivery

request.description:
Send a finished delivery's event again, as a new delivery.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/replay`

Queues a new delivery of a `done` or `parked` delivery's event: same `event_id` (so the same
`webhook-id` header, which receivers deduplicate on) and same payload. The new delivery
has `replay_of` set and its own attempts; the original keeps its history. One still pending
or running is a 409. At most 10 replays of an endpoint wait at once; more is a 429.

Send a finished delivery again.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/retry`

A `done` or `parked` delivery is sent again from its first attempt, with its original
`webhook-id` and payload. One still pending or running is a 409.

The user's provider connections.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/connections`

item.name: How up to date each of the user's sources is

request.description:
How up to date each of the user's sources is.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/freshness`

One entry per provider connection, then one per device source (Apple Health) that uploaded,
ordered by provider. `synced_through` is the end of the most recent window pulled (the time of
the last upload for a device source) and `lag_seconds` is how far behind now it is. Providers
that send notifications are pulled within seconds of a change; the regular pull is a backstop,
every 6 hours while notifications arrive (`push_healthy`) and every hour otherwise.
`state` is `fresh`, `stale` (behind by more than two pull intervals, or no upload for 26 hours),
`failing` (the last 3 pulls failed, see `last_error`), `syncing` (first pull not done),
`needs_reauth` or `disconnected`.

Start connecting a provider.

`POST /v1/users/{id}/connections/{provider}`

Returns the provider's consent URL. Send the user there; after consent the user
lands on `redirect_uri?status=connected|error&provider=<slug>`, or on a built-in
result page when no `redirect_uri` is given. Each call mints a fresh single-use state;
`Idempotency-Key` is not honoured here. While the user's data from this provider is
being deleted the answer is 409: connect again once the deletion job is done.

variable.description: Connector slug, see GET /v1/providers.

request.description:
Disconnect a provider.

`DELETE /v1/users/{id}/connections/{provider}`

Revokes the provider grant (best effort) and stops pulling. By default the data
already collected is kept (204).

With `delete_data=true` the user's data from this provider is erased too: the
disconnect happens at once, then a background job deletes every record, raw file and
sync record of this user and provider (the user and their other providers stay). The
answer is 202 with the `job_id` to poll at `GET /v1/deletions/{job_id}`; asking again
while it runs returns the same job. Until it is done the provider cannot be connected
again and its uploads are refused. The `data.erased` webhook announces the end.

query.description: true also erases the data the user holds from this provider.

variable.description: Connector slug, see GET /v1/providers.

item.name: Create a link to the hosted connection page

request.description:
Create a link to the hosted connection page.

`POST /v1/users/{id}/connect-sessions`

Returns a link to a page served by Open Health Sync where the user picks a provider and goes
through its consent, so your app needs no connection UI of its own. The token in the link is
the page's only credential: send the link to this user only. It serves several providers
until `expires_at`. After each consent the user lands on
`redirect_uri?status=connected|error&provider=<slug>`, or, without `redirect_uri`, on the
built-in result page, which links back to the connection page. See docs/connect-page.md.

Sync a connection now.

`POST /v1/users/{id}/connections/{provider}/sync`

Queues a pull of the connection ahead of routine work and answers with the sync run; follow it
at the `Location` header. The window ends now and starts where the connection's data ends
(minus an hour of overlap), a day back for a connection that never synced, or at `from`
(at most 30 days back). While a manual run of the connection is still queued or running, the
answer is 200 with that run and nothing new is queued. 409 when the connection does not sync
(`needs_reauth`, `disconnected`: connect the user again) or its provider is not enabled here.

variable.description: Connector slug, see GET /v1/providers.

request.description:
The user's sync history.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/sync-runs`

Every pull of the user's connections, newest first: what started it, its window, its status,
the raw payloads it stored and the provider's error when it failed. Finished runs are kept
30 days.

query.description: Only this provider's runs.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

Every source the user has recorded consent for, with the state of each data
category, and the list of categories. A source with no consent recorded stores
everything, unless the instance sets `OHS_CONSENT_REQUIRED=true`, where it stores

item.name: Set the categories the user allows from a source

request.description:
Set the categories the user allows from a source.

`PUT /v1/users/{id}/consents/{provider}`

`granted` becomes the whole list: every category left out is revoked. From then on
the source's records outside `granted` are dropped before they are stored, and the
records already stored in a revoked category are deleted in the background. Each
change is kept in the history and announced by the `consent.granted` and
`consent.revoked` webhooks. Raw payloads are not split by category: they follow
`OHS_RETENTION_DAYS` and the user's erasure.

Daily summaries.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/daily`

item.name: Heart rate variability derived from the RR intervals

request.description:
Heart rate variability derived from the RR intervals.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/hrv`

One record per heartbeat series: the time domain HRV measures (RMSSD, SDNN, pNN50) and the
mean RR interval and heart rate, computed from the stored intervals after implausible and
ectopic intervals are set aside. Ordered by the series' first beat, then provider and
series id. A series is in `[start, end)` when its first beat is, and is always summarized
whole. See docs/hrv.md for the rules.

query.description: Keep one heartbeat series.
Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

item.name: Menstrual cycles derived from the recorded flow

request.description:
Menstrual cycles derived from the recorded flow.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/menstrual-cycles`

Derived at read time from the `menstrual_flow` category samples, so it always agrees with
them, deletions included. A flow day is a local calendar day (the sample's `timezone`
metadata, else UTC) with a flow sample whose label is not `none`; a period is a run of
flow days with gaps of at most 2 days; a cycle runs from a period's first day to the day
before the next period's first day, and the latest cycle is open (`end_date` and
`cycle_length_days` null). Intermenstrual bleeding never starts a period. Nothing is
predicted. `start` and `end` compare as dates and select cycles by `start_date`. A call
reads at most 50000 flow samples: a page can then hold fewer than `limit` cycles and
still carry a `next_cursor`. See docs/menstrual-cycles.md.

query.description: Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

item.name: The order of sources the merged view ranks by

request.description:
The order of sources the merged view ranks by.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/source-priorities`

The user's own orders, keyed by metric (a quantity type, `sleep` or `workouts`), by
group (`activity`, `heart`, `recovery`, `body`, `sleep`, `workouts`) or `*` for every
metric, and the built-in orders that apply where the user set none. The most specific
order wins: metric, then group, then the user's `*`, then the built-in group order. A
source missing from an order ranks after every listed one. See docs/data-model.md.

item.name: Replace the user's orders of sources

request.description:
Replace the user's orders of sources.

`PUT /v1/users/{id}/source-priorities`

Replaces every order of the user; `{"priorities": {}}` goes back to the built-in
orders. Source names are lowercased. Stored records are never changed: the orders
only decide what the merged view shows.

item.name: What has landed, per provider and day, and what is still processing

request.description:
What has landed, per provider and day, and what is still processing.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/coverage`

Record counts per provider per local day, and `pending_jobs`, the user's ETL jobs not
finished yet. After an upload, poll until `pending_jobs` is 0 to know every part has
been processed; then `rejected_records` above 0 means some lines were not stored.
Not paged: at most 10000 days are returned, the earliest, and
`truncated` is true when more matched (narrow `start` and `end`). `start` and `end`
compare as dates.

query.description: Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.

`merged` (the default): when several sources recorded the same thing (a ring and a
watch the same night, a phone and a watch the same steps, one sample directly and
through an aggregator), only the best ranked source's record is listed, so nothing
counts twice. The order of sources is the user's (see source-priorities). `all`:
every stored record of every source.

request.description:
Record a time tag.

`POST /v1/users/{id}/tags`

A time tag is an interval that gives context to the user's data: an illness, a trip,
jet lag, a vaccination. It is context only: nothing is computed from it. `end_at`
absent or null is a tag still ongoing; close it later with PATCH. `start_at` and
`end_at` take an RFC 3339 time or a `YYYY-MM-DD` date (midnight UTC). `label` and
`note` are free text and are treated as health data: never logged. See
docs/time-tags.md.

header.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and the same request gets the first response back.

request.description:
The user's time tags.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/tags`

By `start_at`, then id. With `start` and `end`, the tags that overlap the window
`[start, end)`: a tag `[start_at, end_at)` is listed when `start_at < end` and
`end_at > start`, and an ongoing tag (`end_at` null) when `start_at < end`. A tag that
ends exactly at `start`, or starts exactly at `end`, does not overlap. `start` equal to
`end` is an empty window.

query.description: Only the tags of this kind. Another value is a 400.
Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

request.description:
One time tag.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/tags/{tag_id}`

variable.description: The `id` of a time tag of this user.

request.description:
Change a time tag.

`PATCH /v1/users/{id}/tags/{tag_id}`

Absent members stay as they are; null clears `label`, `timezone`, `note` or `end_at`
(null `end_at` reopens the tag). `kind` and `start_at` cannot be null, and `source`
cannot change. The tag after the change is checked as a whole: `end_at` must stay after
`start_at`. A body that changes nothing returns the tag as it is.

variable.description: The `id` of a time tag of this user.

request.description:
Delete a time tag.

`DELETE /v1/users/{id}/tags/{tag_id}`

variable.description: The `id` of a time tag of this user.

item.name: The user's records as FHIR R4 Observations

request.description:
The user's records as FHIR R4 Observations.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Observation`

The user's records as one FHIR R4 (4.0.1) `searchset` Bundle of Observations,
`Content-Type: application/fhir+json`: quantity samples (`qs-` ids), blood pressure
panels pairing a systolic and a diastolic sample (`bp-`), sleep sessions (`sleep-`),
workouts (`workout-`) and daily summaries (`daily-`), merged in time order (a
sample's start, a bedtime, a workout's start, a day at midnight UTC), then by kind
and id. Paged like every list: the Bundle's `next` link carries the cursor, and
there is no `next` link on the last page; `total` is left out. A blood pressure pair
is never split across pages, and its two samples are not listed on their own.
Vital signs meet the R4 vital signs profiles they claim in `meta.profile`. The
mapping (codes, units, categories, provenance and limits) is in docs/fhir.md. In the
merged view (the default) a record another source covers better is left out, and a
daily summary keeps only the figures it owns (see `view`). The
filters below combine: a record is listed when it matches all of them. Errors are
`application/problem+json` like the rest of the API.

query.description:
Canonical quantity type, for example heart_rate: only quantity samples of that
type, and the blood pressure panels holding a sample of it. Optional; a name
outside the quantity type catalog is a 400 (unless this user has samples of it).

A FHIR token `system|code` matched against `Observation.code`: a LOINC code
(`http://loinc.org|8867-4`; 85354-9, 8480-6 and 8462-4 find the blood pressure
panels, 93832-4 the sleep sessions, 55411-3 the workouts), a quantity type
(`https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/fhir/CodeSystem/quantity-type|heart_rate`,
like `type`), or a record type
(`https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/fhir/CodeSystem/record-type|`
`blood_pressure`, `sleep_session`, `workout` or `daily_summary`). One value; other
systems are a 400. A code no Observation carries is an empty Bundle.

An HL7 observation category code, bare or as
`http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/observation-category|code`: `vital-signs`,
`laboratory` or `activity` (activity samples, workouts and daily summaries). One
value. Another code of that system is an empty Bundle; anything else is a 400.
Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.

`merged` (the default): when several sources recorded the same thing (a ring and a
watch the same night, a phone and a watch the same steps, one sample directly and
through an aggregator), only the best ranked source's record is listed, so nothing
counts twice. The order of sources is the user's (see source-priorities). `all`:
every stored record of every source.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

request.description:
One FHIR R4 Observation.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Observation/{observation_id}`

The Observation an entry's `fullUrl` points to. Not the user's, not an id of these
forms, or not of that shape (`qs-` of a sample that is half of a blood pressure
panel, `bp-` of a sample that is not) is a 404. In the merged view (the default) a
daily summary carries only the figures no better ranked source of the day holds.

query.description:
`merged` (the default): when several sources recorded the same thing (a ring and a
watch the same night, a phone and a watch the same steps, one sample directly and
through an aggregator), only the best ranked source's record is listed, so nothing
counts twice. The order of sources is the user's (see source-priorities). `all`:
every stored record of every source.

variable.description:
The Observation id, as the Bundle gives it: `qs-`, `bp-` (the systolic sample's
id), `sleep-`, `workout-` or `daily-`, then the stored row id.

item.name: The user as a FHIR R4 Patient

request.description:
The user as a FHIR R4 Patient.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Patient/{patient_id}`

The user as a Patient: `id` is the user id, `active` is true, and `identifier` is the
tenant's `external_ref` when it set one. No name or birth date (not stored). A
`patient_id` other than the user's id, or a user of another tenant, is a 404.

variable.description: The Patient id, which is the user id; any other value is a 404.

item.name: The Patient and all their records, as FHIR R4 resources

request.description:
The Patient and all their records, as FHIR R4 resources.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Patient/{patient_id}/$everything`

One page of a `searchset` Bundle: on the first page the Patient, then the page's
Observations (`search.mode` `match`, the list and the cursor of the Observation
search), then the Devices they reference (each once per page) and the Provenance of
each Observation (`include`). Follow the `next` link until there is none: no
Observation is skipped or repeated. `limit` counts the Observations. See docs/fhir.md.

query.description: Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

`merged` (the default): when several sources recorded the same thing (a ring and a
watch the same night, a phone and a watch the same steps, one sample directly and
through an aggregator), only the best ranked source's record is listed, so nothing
counts twice. The order of sources is the user's (see source-priorities). `all`:
every stored record of every source.

variable.description: The Patient id, which is the user id; any other value is a 404.

item.name: The devices the user's records came from, as FHIR R4 Devices

request.description:
The devices the user's records came from, as FHIR R4 Devices.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Device`

A `searchset` Bundle of the devices named by the provenance of the user's quantity
samples, sleep sessions and workouts whose time is in the window, each once, in one
page (no `next` link). Unbounded, it reads the provenance of every record of the user:
pass `start` and `end` on a large history. `cursor` and `limit` are a 400.

query.description: Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.

request.description:
One FHIR R4 Device.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Device/{device_id}`

The Device an Observation references. A device none of the user's records names is a
404.

variable.description: The Device id, as an Observation's `device.reference` gives it.

request.description:
The Provenance of one Observation.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Provenance`

A `searchset` Bundle holding the Provenance of the Observation `target` names, or no
entry when the user has no such Observation.

query.description: `Observation/` and an Observation id. One value.

request.description:
One FHIR R4 Provenance.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/Provenance/{provenance_id}`

The Provenance of one Observation; an Observation that does not exist is a 404.

variable.description: `prov-` and the id of the Observation it is about.

item.name: The FHIR R4 CapabilityStatement of the user's FHIR base

request.description:
The FHIR R4 CapabilityStatement of the user's FHIR base.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/fhir/metadata`

What the FHIR routes serve (read only), as a CapabilityStatement.

item.name: The user's records as Open mHealth data points

request.description:
The user's records as Open mHealth data points.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/omh/data-points`

The user's records as Open mHealth data points (a `header` and a `body` that follows one
schema of the Open mHealth catalog, checked against the official schemas): heart rate,
steps, blood pressure, body weight, height, BMI, body fat, body temperature, oxygen
saturation, respiratory rate, blood glucose and active energy samples, sleep sessions
(`sleep-episode`) and workouts (`physical-activity`). In the order and with the cursor of
the FHIR search; a record without an Open mHealth schema (another quantity type, a
daily summary, a value in another unit) is left out, so a page can hold fewer than
`limit` data points and still have a `next_cursor`. The mapping is in
docs/open-mhealth.md.

query.description:
Only the data points of one schema, bare (`heart-rate`) or with its namespace and,
optionally, its version (`omh:heart-rate`, `omh:heart-rate:2.0`). One value; a
schema the mapping does not emit is a 400.
Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.
The next_cursor of the previous page.

`merged` (the default): when several sources recorded the same thing (a ring and a
watch the same night, a phone and a watch the same steps, one sample directly and
through an aggregator), only the best ranked source's record is listed, so nothing
counts twice. The order of sources is the user's (see source-priorities). `all`:
every stored record of every source.

item.name: One list of the user as a CSV or Parquet file

request.description:
One list of the user as a CSV or Parquet file.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/exports/{dataset}`

Every record of one list in `[start, end)`, as one file streamed in a single response
(`Content-Disposition: attachment`). The columns are the members of the list's JSON
records, in the same order and with the same names and values: times in UTC, a missing
value empty (CSV) or null (Parquet), `metadata` (and the daily `sources`) as JSON text. `samples` holds every
quantity type unless `type` names one. The file is not paged: `cursor` and `limit` are
a 400. A failure once the file has started cuts the connection, so a truncated file
never looks complete. See docs/exports.md.

query.description: `csv` (the default) or `parquet`.
The canonical type to keep, for the lists that have one (samples, category-samples, workouts).
Inclusive lower bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD.
Exclusive upper bound, RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start.

variable.description: The list to export. Another name is a 404.

item.name: Everything held about one user, as one zip file

request.description:
Everything held about one user, as one zip file.

`GET /v1/users/{id}/archive`

The answer to a data portability request: one zip file streamed in a single response
(`Content-Disposition: attachment`) holding `manifest.json` (user, generation time,
instance version, record count of each file, a description of each folder),
`user.json` (the user and its provider connections, never a token),
`canonical/<list>.ndjson` (every record of samples, category-samples, sleep,
sleep-phases, workouts, workout-routes, nutrition and daily, the same JSON as the list
items, one per line), `fhir/bundle.json` (a FHIR R4 `collection` Bundle of every
Observation), `omh/data-points.ndjson` (the Open mHealth data points) and `raw/...`
(every raw payload of the user, byte for byte, under its path below the user). A
tenant key reads any user of the tenant; a user token with scope `read` reads only its
own user, and another user is a 404. A failure once the file has started cuts the
connection, so a truncated archive never looks complete. See docs/exports.md.

item.name: Upload one part of an Apple Health export

request.description:
Upload one part of an Apple Health export.

`POST /v1/ingest/apple-health`

One gzip NDJSON part (at most 64 MiB, never truncated), one data type per part.
Re-sending the same part is safe: the answer is 200 with `duplicate: true`. Other
bytes under a (day, batch, part) already stored are a 409, and so is a part sent while
this provider's data is being deleted for the user (nothing is kept; send it again
once the deletion job is done). Each instance processes a
bounded number of uploads at once; above it the answer is 503 with `Retry-After`.

Needs a user token (ohs_ut_) as the client's apiKey.

header.description: HealthKit type identifier of every line of the part.

item.name: Upload one part of Android Health Connect records

request.description:
Upload one part of Android Health Connect records.

`POST /v1/ingest/health-connect`

One gzip NDJSON part (at most 64 MiB, never truncated), one Health Connect record per
line, each a JSON object with a `recordType` (the line format is in
docs/connectors/health-connect.md). Same headers, limits and answers as the Apple Health
upload.
Re-sending the same part is safe: the answer is 200 with `duplicate: true`. Other
bytes under a (day, batch, part) already stored are a 409, and so is a part sent while
this provider's data is being deleted for the user (nothing is kept; send it again
once the deletion job is done). Each instance processes a
bounded number of uploads at once; above it the answer is 503 with `Retry-After`.

Needs a user token (ohs_ut_) as the client's apiKey.

header.description: Health Connect record type of the lines of the part (for example BloodGlucose).

item.name: The tenant's audit log, newest first

request.description:
The tenant's audit log, newest first.

`GET /v1/audit`

One event per authenticated request (tenant key or user token) and per
administrative or system action: who (the credential), what (the action
and route), about which user, when, and the status. Never a health value,
a secret or a query string. Append only; events older than
`OHS_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 365) are pruned.

query.description: Only events about this end user.
An exact action (`data.export`), or a prefix ending in a dot (`data.`).
Events at or after this time (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD).
Events before this time (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD).
The next_cursor of the previous page.
